rules.instruction: When the description says a receipt (a start or arrival of information or items) is followed by an action the company itself performs on the work, such as determining details, ordering from several sources in parallel, or inspecting and assembling, and the description states the arrival of the resulting items as a separate later occurrence: Model the receipt only as the start event or intermediate catch event for that occurrence. Model each stated company action as its own task (use a service task if the description says it is performed by a system or external source, otherwise a user task), placed in the order the description gives: directly after the receiving element, and before any parallel split or join that the description puts around it. When the description says several such actions run in parallel, place them after one parallel split and join them before the next step. Model a later arrival of items as an intermediate catch event that only represents the wait, and keep it separate from the company's action on those items. Do not let the receipt event or the arrival event replace or absorb a stated action, and do not drop an action because a related event already appears in the model.
rules.situation: the description says a receipt (a start or arrival of information or items) is followed by an action the company itself performs on the work, such as determining details, ordering from several sources in parallel, or inspecting and assembling, and the description states the arrival of the resulting items as a separate later occurrence

rules.instruction: When the description says that parallel work can begin only after an external party has provided information, and that the process itself then works on that information before the parallel activities start: Do not make the external party's provision of the information the start event. Model the process's own step of determining or recording that information as a task placed before the split into parallel activities, and attach the start event to the process's own trigger. Use a start event for the provision only if the description names it as the process trigger.
rules.situation: the description says that parallel work can begin only after an external party has provided information, and that the process itself then works on that information before the parallel activities start

rules.instruction: When the description says a work item is initiated (for example, requests are sent to external parties) and its result is only awaited later, possibly in parallel with other work: Model the initiating work as its own task in the flow, placed before any parallel split that runs it alongside other work. Model the later awaited result as a separate intermediate catch event that follows, and do not let the catch event replace the initiating task.
rules.situation: the description says a work item is initiated (for example, requests are sent to external parties) and its result is only awaited later, possibly in parallel with other work

rules.instruction: When the description says a participant itself carries out a named check or inspection of received material as a step placed between two other steps, and names no message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for for that step: Model that step as a bpmn:userTask performed by the participant, placed in the sequence where the description places it, and labelled with the action verb and object the description states. Do not model it as a bpmn:manualTask, and do not add a second element for the same step.
rules.situation: the description says a participant itself carries out a named check or inspection of received material as a step placed between two other steps, and names no message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for for that step

rules.instruction: When the description says several activities are started together in parallel and a later activity begins only after all of them are finished, including branches where a wait for an external delivery is followed by a person's check: Make the parallel split start every branch, and send the last element of every branch, including the activity that follows the wait, into the same parallel join gateway before the shared continuation. Do not leave any parallel branch without an outgoing flow to that join, and do not replace the join with an exclusive gateway.
rules.situation: the description says several activities are started together in parallel and a later activity begins only after all of them are finished, including branches where a wait for an external delivery is followed by a person's check
